history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset: Ajmer Sharif Dargah is the tomb (dargah) of the Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (also called Gharib Nawaz, 'Benefactor of the Poor'), founder of the Chishti order in India, who came to Ajmer from Persia in the 12th century and died in 1236 CE. His followers built the shrine after his death; Sultan Ghiyasuddin Khilji of Malwa built the main tomb in the 15th century, and Mughal emperors Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb expanded it with gates, mosques (including the Akbari Mosque) and courtyards. Notable features include the pair of huge cooking vessels (degs) associated with Akbar and Jahangir, used to prepare food distributed as tabarruk. The six-day Urs festival in Rajab draws lakhs of pilgrims of all faiths, with qawwali, langar and the ghusal ritual (washing of the tomb with rose water and sandalwood paste). No CSV correction needed: town Ajmer, district Ajmer, state Rajasthan are correct.

name: Ajmer Sharif Dargah
town_description: Ajmer is a major pilgrimage and heritage city in Rajasthan, home to both the Ajmer Sharif Dargah and, 15 km away, Pushkar's Brahma temple. It grew around the Sufi shrine and the 12th-century Taragarh Fort.
tradition: Islam (Sufi, Chishtiya order) - NOT a Hindu temple; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport is the nearest major airport (~135 km); Kishangarh (Ajmer) airport serves limited flights.
travel.railway: Ajmer Junction is a major railway station on the Delhi-Mumbai and Jaipur-Ahmedabad routes.
travel.road: Well connected by road from Jaipur (~135 km), Pushkar (~15 km) and Delhi (~400 km); the dargah is in the old city near Dargah Bazaar.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer: 4:00 AM to 10:00 PM; Winter: 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM. Dress modestly, cover the head, remove shoes, and avoid photography inside the shrine.
